extracted.intended_audience: Prospective ONR/DoD grant applicants (universities, nonprofits, companies) preparing proposals for BAA N00014-23-S-B001
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation/administrative requirements for preparing and submitting a technical proposal and associated forms for ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B001, including proposal structure, budgets, compliance certifications, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and Representations (SF-424 / Financial Assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17, the applicant certifies the statements contained in the list of certifications and that the statements are true, complete and accurate to the best of their knowledge; provide required assurances and agree to comply with resulting terms if awarded. False statements may subject the signer to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Financial Assistance General Certifications and Representations must be completed in SAM.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a material representation of fact; required documentation (e.g., SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities) and disclosures (unpaid delinquent tax liability, felony convictions) must be submitted as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 19 – Authorized Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Email address entered by the grantee on the SF424 application to create the EDA notification profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be the same person who signs the SF424 (i.e., the Authorized Organization Representative/AOR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Must identify the research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only characters available on a standard QWERTY keyboard; spell out Greek and other non-English letters/symbols; graphics are not allowed; one page or 4,000-character (including spaces) limit, whichever is less; do not include proprietary/confidential information; must be marked 'Approved for Public Release.' Abstracts of funded projects will be posted on DTIC public site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subject Use (Fields 1 and 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must address human subject involvement by completing Fields 1 and 1a of the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals that include or may include 'research involving human subjects' as defined in DoDI 3216.02, prior to award the applicant must submit required documentation under 'Use of Human Subjects in Research' (Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Use (Fields 2 and 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must address animal use protocols in Fields 2 and 2a of the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animals are to be utilized, the applicant must submit the documents described under 'Use of Animals' (Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Compliance (Fields 4a–4d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether intended research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory and how the applicant will ensure compliance with environmental statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies must comply with environmental planning requirements (e.g., NEPA). Many ONR field research activities are covered by NEPA categorical exclusions; questions should be referred to the technical point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 7 – Project Summary/Abstract submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave Field 7 blank; complete Form SF424, Project Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Grants.gov produces an error when leaving Block 7 blank, upload the Project Abstract instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 8 – Project Narrative (attach full technical proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe clearly the research, including the objective and approach, keeping in mind the evaluation criteria. Attach the entire proposal narrative to R&R Other Project Information form in Field 8 as a single PDF named 'Technical Proposal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technical proposal must describe the research in the sections specified below (Cover Page, Table of Contents, Technical Approach, Future Naval Relevance, Project Schedule and Milestones, Reports, Management Approach, Principal Investigator Qualifications, Responsibility, Data Management Plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover page must include the words 'Technical Proposal' and: (a) BAA Number: N00014-23-S-B001; (b) Title of Proposal; (c) Identity of prime Offeror and complete list of subawards, if applicable; (d) Technical contact (name, address, phone/fax, email); (e) Administrative/business contact (name, address, phone/fax, email); (f) Proposed period of performance (identify both base period and any options, if included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exactly required elements; label clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An alphabetical/numerical listing of the sections within the proposal, including corresponding page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate page numbers to allow reviewers to find sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scientific or technical concepts to be investigated, providing the complete research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what is innovative about the proposed approach, compare to alternate approaches other researchers have taken, and, given successful completion, describe expected results, new knowledge, or insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future Naval Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of potential Naval relevance and contributions of the effort to the agency’s specific mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect proposed research outcomes to Navy/Marine Corps Science & Technology objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Schedule and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of the schedule of events and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, realistic milestones tied to tasks and deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample reports typically required: Technical and Financial Progress Reports and Final Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants do not include delivery of software, prototypes, and other hardware deliverables unless explicitly specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the overall management approach and provide rationale for participation of key team members; describe planned relationships with any subawardees or collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a single-PI award; if subawardees/collaborators are included, explain how the team fits the single PI structure; briefly describe anticipated schedule if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the qualifications of the proposed Principal Investigator and any other key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant experience, prior successes, and specific skills that support project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility information for offeror evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must provide information to assist ONR's evaluation of responsibility, including adequacy of resources, ability to comply with grant conditions given existing commitments, performance history managing federal awards, record of integrity and business ethics, qualifications and eligibility under applicable laws/regulations, and organizational/operational controls and technical skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions of resource availability or ability to obtain resources, accounting and operational controls, property control systems, quality assurance measures, and safety programs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: In no more than 2 pages, describe which data generated will be shared and preserved, how it will be done, or explain why sharing/preservation is not possible or appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address: types of data/software/materials; how data will be acquired; time/location of acquisition if pertinent; how data will be processed; file formats and naming conventions; QA/QC measures; dataset origin when using existing resources; standards for data/metadata format and content; appropriate timeframe for preservation; balance of preservation value vs cost/administrative burden with justification; include a statement if data cannot be made public for national security or Controlled Unclassified Information concerns (cite DoD Instruction 5230.09).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 9 – Bibliography & References
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload your Bibliography/References Cited as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach under the specified field in the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 10 – Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities available for performing the proposed research and any additional facilities the applicant proposes to acquire at its own expense; indicate government-owned facilities already possessed that will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 11 – Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any equipment available or any additional equipment proposed to be acquired at the applicant's expense; indicate government-owned equipment that will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify the need for each equipment item and provide vendor quotes. General purpose equipment (e.g., personal computers) should not be requested unless used primarily/exclusively for the project; include statement on how each item will be integrated into the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Grants.gov Research & Related Budget (R&R) Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Offeror must use the Grants.gov forms including the SF Research and Related (R&R) Budget Form from the application package template associated with this BAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If options are proposed, provide pricing for option periods or options will not be included in the award. Include a separate PDF Budget Justification under Section K and a link to the current single audit report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Direct Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Itemize individual labor categories or persons, with associated labor hours and unburdened direct labor rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide escalation rates for out years; round all costs to the nearest dollar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Administrative and Clerical Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and clerical salaries are normally indirect costs and included in an indirect cost rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct charging may be appropriate only when a major project requires extensive administrative/clerical support significantly greater than normal; direct charges must be supported with a budget justification that adequately describes the major project and the administrative/clerical work to be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Fringe Benefits and Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the rates and calculation of the costs for each rate category (F&A, Overhead, G&A, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rates are negotiated by a government agency, provide memorandum/agreement. Entities without negotiated rates may elect to charge a de minimis rate of 10% of modified total direct costs (see 2 CFR 200.414(f)) or provide sufficient detail for allowability, allocability, and reasonableness. If composite rates are used, provide calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Travel
rubrics_metrics.description: For each trip include the purpose, origin and destination if known, approximate duration, number of travelers, and estimated cost per trip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify costs based on organization's historical average cost per trip or other reasonable basis; estimates must conform to applicable Federal cost principles. May include PI travel to peer review meetings described in Section II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Subawards/Subcontracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description of the work to be performed by the subrecipient/subcontractor and a detailed cost proposal for each subaward submitted by the subrecipient using the R&R budget form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include subrecipient name at top of budget justification. Subcontractor proposals/supporting documentation must be provided for Government cost analysis. Preferred method is to include subcontract information with the prime's proposal; alternatives: sealed envelope or email to Program Officer at time of prime submission (identify proposal title and prime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a breakdown of consultant hours, the hourly rate proposed, any other proposed consultant costs, and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach signed Consulting Agreement or other documentation supporting proposed consultant rate/cost and a copy of the consultant's proposed statement of work if not already identified in prime proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Materials & Supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all proposed materials and supplies including quantities, unit prices, and the basis for the estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis may include quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Recipient Acquired Equipment or Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If acquisition of equipment and/or facilities is proposed, provide a justification and an itemized list of all costs and basis for estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable items are normally limited to research equipment not already available for the project. General purpose equipment should not be requested unless used primarily or exclusively for the project; justify integration into research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Other Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all proposed other direct costs such as Graduate Assistant tuition, laboratory fees, report and publication costs, and the basis for the estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quotes, prior purchases, catalog prices, or other justification as basis for estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/Workshop Funding Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposal requests funds for hosting or attending a conference, workshop or symposium: (1) ONR will not sponsor an ONR, Navy, or DoD event; provide a list of other sponsors and requested amounts; (2) ONR funds generally may not be used to pay for food or beverages as a direct cost except in exceptional circumstances; (3) specify how the event and outcomes directly relate to the US Naval or Marine Corps S&T Plan and identify specific focus areas addressed and desired outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for food/beverages must be fully supported factually in accordance with applicable OMB cost principles and determined reasonable and allowable by the Grants Officer. Desired outcomes examples: conference proceedings, journal articles, algorithms, tools, additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee/Profit Prohibition for Assistance Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee/profit is unallowable under assistance agreements at either the prime or subaward level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee/profit may be permitted on contracts issued by the prime awardee, but not under assistance agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) data
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect degree type and degree year; current and pending support shall list all current projects and future support regardless of source, including title/objectives, percent per year devoted, total amount of support, name and address of sponsors, and period of performance; upload biosketch/CV/resume to the Biographical Sketch field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional senior/key persons can be added. Although some forms may pass Grants.gov edit checks without these fields, ONR may determine an application incomplete if required information is missing and return it without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Personal Data (Demographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form used by ONR as source of demographic information (gender, race, ethnicity, disability) for PD/PI and other key personnel; name fields must be completed, demographic data is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demographic information is used for statistical purposes only; it may be accessible to the reviewer but will not be considered in evaluation. Applicants choosing not to provide may select 'Do not wish to provide.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov Registration Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit applications online through Grants.gov; organizations must have active SAM registration and a Grants.gov account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SAM registration and Grants.gov account before deadlines. Steps: Register with SAM; create Grants.gov account; add a profile (use UEI for organizational profile); EBiz POC must authorize roles (including AOR) to allow submissions; track role status. SAM registration may take additional time—start early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Signature and AOR Role
rubrics_metrics.description: When applications are submitted through Grants.gov, the name of the organization applicant with the AOR role that submitted the application is inserted into the signature line, serving as the electronic signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBiz POC must authorize personnel with the AOR role; authorized signatories must be able to make legally binding commitments on behalf of the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission via Grants.gov Workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use Grants.gov Workspace to apply, which is a shared online environment for teams to access and edit webforms and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a Workspace, add participants, complete required forms, check for errors. You may download PDF forms and use Adobe Reader. Mandatory fields are marked. Complete SF-424 fields first as they populate other forms. Submit at least 48 hours prior to close date to allow time for technical issues. After submission, a Grants.gov Tracking Number is generated; use it to track application.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Format for Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments to grant applications submitted through Grants.gov must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals with attachments submitted in any format other than PDF will not be considered for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Papers submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers must be submitted through FedConnect (as specified elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely Receipt Requirements and Proof of Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic date/time stamp is generated when Grants.gov successfully receives the application; the AOR who submitted will receive acknowledgement and Grants.gov Tracking Number which serves as proof of timely submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR's official proof of timely submission is the date/time that Grants.gov receives the application. Applications received by Grants.gov after the due date will be considered late and not considered for funding. Applicants should allow time for transmission, especially with slow internet. Obtain Grants.gov Support Center ticket numbers if encountering submission problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Support and Troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov provides 24/7 support via toll-free number and email; for specific grant questions contact the number listed in the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If experiencing submission difficulties, call Grants.gov Support and obtain a ticket number to assist ONR in tracking and resolving issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Qualifications (32 CFR 22.415 standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified, a potential recipient must: (1) Have management capability and adequate financial and technical resources to execute the program of activities envisioned; (2) Have a satisfactory record of executing such programs or activities; (3) Have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; (4) Be otherwise qualified and eligible to receive a grant or cooperative agreement under applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submissions to assist the Grants Officer's evaluation of recipient qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS / Integrity & Performance Information
rubrics_metrics.description: For Federal awards with total Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, the awarding agency will review and consider information about the applicant in the designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM (currently FAPIIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may review and comment on information about themselves in FAPIIS; the agency will consider applicant comments along with other information when assessing applicant risk per 2 CFR 200.206.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFATA (Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act) Reporting Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities that apply as prime or sub-recipient under this BAA must provide information in their proposal describing the processes and systems in place to comply with subaward and executive total compensation reporting requirements as codified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies; refer to 2 CFR Part 170 (including Appendix A) for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Restrictions on Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants, cooperative agreements, and TIA awards greater than $100,000 require certification of compliance regarding lobbying; applicants shall provide this certification by electronic submission of SF424 (R&R) (complete Block 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification states no Federal appropriated funds have been/will be paid for influencing federal officers/employees or Members of Congress; if non-federal funds have been/will be paid to influence, submit SF-LLL. The language must be included in award documents for all subawards and subrecipients must certify accordingly. Failure to file the required certification carries civil penalties of $10,000–$100,000 per failure (31 U.S.C. 1352).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Prohibition on Using Funds with Entities that Require Certain Internal Confidentiality Agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, by checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17, certify to statements in the certifications list and that those statements are true, complete, and accurate; the certification includes the supplement (GIC 19-02) regarding entities requiring certain internal confidentiality agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is a material representation of fact upon which reliance is placed when entering into the transaction; applicants must submit any related documentation as applicable. (Full GIC 19-02 text and implications referenced in Section F.)
